faqs.question: How can I track my Diwali expenses across Google Pay, PhonePe, and Paytm in one place?

Pocket Advisor securely monitors these SMS alerts on-device, extracting the merchant name, amount, and account to update a unified festive dashboard in real time.

faqs.question: Does Pocket Advisor require netbanking passwords, bank logins, or OTPs?
faqs.answer: No. Pocket Advisor never asks for bank account numbers, passwords, OTPs, or UPI PINs. All spending analysis happens strictly from local transaction SMS records stored natively on your phone without uploading any data to external servers.

faqs.question: How much of my monthly income should I budget for Diwali?
faqs.answer: Financial planners recommend capping total festive spending between 15% and 20% of your net monthly take-home income (or your earmarked festive bonus). Never compromise your emergency fund or ongoing mutual fund SIP investments for temporary festival shopping.

faqs.question: Can I set separate budget caps for categories like Sweets, Gifts, and Decor?
faqs.answer: Yes. In the Pocket Advisor Android app, you can create dedicated spending buckets and track real-time progress bars to ensure individual festive categories do not exceed your predetermined cap.

faqs.question: Is there any extra fee or MDR charge on UPI transactions this Diwali?
faqs.answer: No. The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) and the Ministry of Finance have confirmed that UPI payments remain 100% free for consumers. While Merchant Discount Rates (MDR) apply to certain commercial accounts, merchants are legally prohibited from passing charges onto consumers.

blocks.text: Diwali spending rarely goes over budget because of one lavish purchase. It usually happens through dozens of seamless digital micro-payments—sweet boxes, decorative fairy lights, delivery tips, gifts, cab rides, and quick QR code scans at roadside stalls.

With over 55.4 crore registered UPI users in India generating over 800 million daily transactions during the peak festive season (NPCI 2026), digital payments have eliminated the physical friction of cash. When tapping your UPI PIN feels identical for a ₹50 chai as it does for a ₹5,000 festive outfit, holiday budgets quietly disappear without notice.

blocks.text: Why UPI Spending Escapes Notice During Festivals

When paying with physical cash, parting with five crisp ₹500 notes triggers immediate cognitive awareness. You feel the physical weight leaving your wallet. With UPI on Google Pay, PhonePe, or Paytm, scanning a QR code produces the exact same instantaneous screen animation whether you spend ₹40 on chai or ₹4,000 on dry fruit hampers.

blocks.title: The "Frictionless Payment" Illusion
blocks.content: Digital payments remove the psychological pain of paying. Because transactions are instantaneous and silent, festive shoppers routinely underestimate their cumulative spending by 30% to 50%.

blocks.text: The 15–20% Income Rule for Diwali Budgeting

Before visiting festive bazaars or browsing e-commerce sales, establish a non-negotiable financial ceiling. Certified financial planners recommend the **15% to 20% Rule**: your total discretionary festive outlays across clothes, gifts, sweets, and celebrations should never exceed 15% to 20% of your take-home monthly salary (or your earmarked festive bonus).

blocks.title: The 3 Golden Budgeting Principles for Diwali
blocks.content:
1. **Bonus Segregation:** Allocate 50% of your festive bonus to savings/debt prepayments, 30% to planned festivities, and 20% to discretionary treats.
2. **Pre-commit Category Caps:** Fix individual limits for sweets, gifts, and decor before stepping into markets.
3. **Dedicated Festive Account:** Move your festive budget to a secondary bank account linked to UPI so your core savings remain protected.

blocks.text: 10 UPI Expenses to Audit Before Diwali

items.text: Online Flash Sales: Check your cart for impulse electronics and decor discounts you didn't plan for.
Quick Grocery Apps: Monitor delivery charges and surge pricing on 10-minute grocery apps (Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart).
Bulk Sweet Hampers: Avoid luxury packaging markups by purchasing curated local mithai.
Cab Surge Pricing: Check ride aggregator surge multipliers during Dhanteras and Diwali eve traffic peaks.
Street Decor Scans: Keep track of small cash/QR scans on diyas, garlands, and fairy lights.
Recurring OTT Subscriptions: Pause unused streaming memberships that auto-renew during holiday week.
Peer Gift Pools: Log shared office gifts and family celebration contributions promptly.
Restaurant & Dining Out: Ensure group party dinners don't exceed your dining bucket.
Dhanteras Gold/Silver: Separate auspicious ceremonial purchases from long-term investment assets.
Unsettled Group Splits: Send UPI settlement requests immediately after shared festive trips.

blocks.text: Guarding Against the "Credit on UPI" & BNPL Trap

A major shift in the 2026 festive season is the rapid expansion of **Credit on UPI** (linking RuPay credit cards to UPI) and Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) checkouts. While convenient, financing perishable festival consumption through revolving debt carries immense danger.

blocks.title: The Perishable Expense Rule
blocks.content: Never borrow money or swipe revolving credit lines for items consumed within 48 hours (sweets, fireworks, decorations). Unpaid festive balances attract annualized interest rates of **36% to 44%**, turning a festive celebration into a months-long financial headache.

blocks.text: Splitting Group Celebrations with Minimal Transfers

When celebrating Diwali with flatmates, friends, or family potlucks, multiple people often pay for different expenses. Rather than executing 15 confusing cross-transfers where everyone pays everyone else, Pocket Advisor's greedy debt engine balances net credits and debits to settle the entire group in just 2 or 3 direct payments.
